edges.description: Reduced CHD2 impairs ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling.
Disrupted chromatin accessibility alters transcription at target genes.
Dysregulated developmental gene expression impairs neuronal maturation.
Dysregulated excitability-gene expression predisposes to seizures.
The abnormal developmental substrate may contribute to regression, although the terminal mechanism is unresolved.
Frequent ongoing epileptiform activity can drive cognitive slowing or regression in CHD2-related epileptic encephalopathy.

nodes.description: Impaired chromatin remodeling changes the transcription of CHD2 target genes, including genes governing neuronal development and neuronal excitability, so that the coordinated gene-expression programs of the developing brain are dysregulated.

evidence.snippet: Chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 2 (CHD2) gene mutations have been  reported in patients with myoclonic-atonic epilepsy (MAE)

nodes.description: Dysregulated expression of genes controlling neuronal excitability shifts the balance between excitation and inhibition in cortical networks, producing neuronal hyperexcitability and hypersynchrony that generate seizures, including photosensitive and myoclonic seizures. Human stem-cell models show that CHD2 loss selectively impairs the maturation of cortical inhibitory (GABAergic) interneurons while sparing excitatory neurons, providing a mechanistic substrate for the excitation-inhibition imbalance.
